newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian court approves "golden share" vote.
newsitem.headline: Italian court approves "golden share" vote.

text.p: Italy's constitutional court on Thursday allowed a proposed referendum seeking to abolish the use of "golden shares" giving the Treasury special powers in privatised companies deemed to be of public interest.
The vote is one of 11 approved by the court.

The golden share issue is of growing significance to investors as the goverment's program of sell-offs gathers pace and the Treasury prepares to merge telecoms group Stet with Telecom Italia in advance of privatisation.

The government has already introduced a golden share provision in the statutes of ENI. Two tranches of shares in the energy group were sold to investors in 1995 and 1996 but the government still retains a majority interest.
The government is also pondering whether to introduce a golden share for Stet which it hopes to privatise this year.
The Communist Refoundation party (RC) has said it is opposed to the government surrendering control of Stet.
The government relies on support from RC in the lower house of parliament where it lacks a majority.
Golden share arrangements are unpopular with institutional investors who say they fear government meddling in corporate management.
